evidence: Since its opening in 1969, the theater has been a beacon of cultural pride, showcasing the enchanting Múa Tiên, or Fairy Dance, which embodies the elegance and grace of Vietnamese traditional arts. This performance is deeply rooted in the legacy of King Lý Thái Tổ, who moved the capital to Thăng Long in the early 11th century, marking the birthplace of a sophisticated art form that emerged from the rich wet rice civilization.

The slender, delicate puppets, adorned in vibrant peach-colored silk, glide gracefully across the water, their glossy lacquered wooden cores catching the light. The highlight of the performance is the rhythmic swaying of soft silk ribbons, which dance fluidly over the rippling waves, creating an ethereal ambiance.
